## Exercise 1 and Exercise 2

```{r}
#' Re-scale a numeric vector to a new target range 
#' 
#' This function re-scales a numeric vector with at least 2 items to a new vector with the same length but different, designated target range. 
#' 
#' @param x a numeric vector to be re-scaled, items cannot all be the same number. 
#' @param y a numeric vector of length 2, indicating the min and max of the target range, respectively. The default is 'c(0,1)'. 
#' @param na.rm a logical parameter indicating if NA values should be removed. The default is 'True'. 
#' @return A numeric vector of the same length as 'x', but with the values scaled according to the values provided in 'y'.

rescale_min_max <- function(x, y = c(0, 1), na.rm = TRUE) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(x), is.numeric(y), length(y) == 2, y[1] < y[2])
  rng <- range(x, na.rm = na.rm)
  if (rng[1] == rng[2]) stop("Cannot rescale a constant number")
  (x - rng[1]) / (rng[2] - rng[1]) * (y[2] - y[1]) + y[1]
}

```

## Exercise 3

Demonstrate the usage of your function with a few examples. Use one or more new code chunks, describing what you’re doing.

```{r}
# rescale a numeric vector
example1 <- c(10,25,40,58)
rescale_min_max(example1)
```

```{r}
# rescale a numeric vector with NA, should get the same length vector
example2 <- c(2, NA, 7, 11, 50)
rescale_min_max(example2)
```

```{r}
# rescale a non-numeric vector, should get error
# example3 <- c("1", "2", "3")
# rescale_min_max(example3)
```

```{r}
# rescale with invalid target interval, should get error 
# example4 <- c(1,3,5)
# rescale_min_max(example4, y = c(20,1))
```

## Exercise 4

```{r}
test_that("rescale_min_max works correctly across all ranges", {
  # default to [0, 1]
  expect_equal(
    rescale_min_max(c(10, 20, 30)),
    c(0, 0.5, 1)
  )

  # negative endpoints -- y[1], y[2]
  expect_equal(
    rescale_min_max(c(0, 5, 10), y = c(-1, 1)),
    c(-1, 0, 1)
  )

  # handling NA 
  expect_equal(
    rescale_min_max(c(1, NA, 3), na.rm = TRUE),
    c(0, NA, 1)
  )
})

# expect errors: 
test_that("rescale_min_max outputs errors correctly", {
  # error on non-numeric x
  expect_error(
    rescale_min_max(c("a", "b", "c")),
    class = "error"
  )

  # error on constant vector (same numbers)
  expect_error(
    rescale_min_max(c(7, 7, 7)),
    "Cannot rescale a constant number"
  )

  # error when target bounds in y are inverted 
  expect_error(
    rescale_min_max(c(1, 2, 3), y = c(5, 1)),
    class = "error"
  )
})
```
